title: Bank of Japan will continue rate hikes to keep inflation at the target
gist: Oxford Economics says the BoJ held at 1.25% in a hawkish pause and will likely hike in December and April to 1.75%. It argues target-level inflation reflects supply-side pass-through more than wage-driven demand, and the BoJ is also speeding up ETF sales.

themes.theme: BoJ hawkish pause and rate path

insights.claim: The Bank of Japan held its policy rate at 1.25% on 30 Oct 2026 in a widely expected 'hawkish pause' that did not change Oxford Economics' near-term forecast.
insights.speaker: Yasuko Koido
insights.so_what: No surprise in the October hold; focus shifts to December.
insights.quote: delivered a ‘hawkish pause’ today, keeping its policy rate at 1.25%

insights.claim: Oxford Economics expects the BoJ to hike in December and April to a terminal rate of 1.75%.
insights.speaker: Yasuko Koido
insights.so_what: Implies two further 25bp hikes; supports yen and pressures JGB yields.

insights.claim: The BoJ said more rate hikes are needed to prevent inflation overshooting the target.
insights.speaker: Yasuko Koido
insights.so_what: Policy bias is tightening, not neutral.

insights.claim: If the supply-side shock lasts longer than expected, the BoJ may need to hike to 2% by July, just before the terms of the two most hawkish board members end, despite rising government pressure.
insights.speaker: Yasuko Koido
insights.so_what: Upside risk to the terminal rate and a possible faster hiking timetable.

insights.claim: BoJ underlying inflation indicators have reached the 2% target, and Governor Ueda says policy focus has shifted from raising inflation to keeping it at 2% as risks are tilted to the upside.
insights.speaker: Yasuko Koido
insights.so_what: Regime shift from reflation to inflation control.

insights.claim: Target-level underlying inflation was driven mainly by pass-through of external supply-side shocks rather than the wage-driven demand growth the government and BoJ pursued.
insights.speaker: Yasuko Koido
insights.so_what: Inflation quality is weaker than headline suggests, raising the risk of policy overtightening.

insights.claim: Domestic demand has been resilient to rate hikes and the terms-of-trade shock but lacks momentum.
insights.speaker: Yasuko Koido
insights.so_what: Limited demand cushion if hikes continue.

insights.claim: Oxford expects the inflation shock from higher energy prices and past yen depreciation to fade gradually, with inflation stabilising around 2% in late 2027.
insights.speaker: Yasuko Koido
insights.so_what: Fading shock caps how far the BoJ needs to go beyond 1.75%.

insights.claim: The BoJ will raise annual sales of its ETF holdings from 330 billion yen to 860 billion yen from 2027.
insights.speaker: Yasuko Koido
insights.so_what: More supply of ETFs into the Japanese equity market, though still small.

insights.claim: The faster ETF sales shorten the time to complete the unwind from about 112 years to 43 years.
insights.speaker: Yasuko Koido
insights.so_what: Even the faster pace implies a decades-long overhang, so the market impact is gradual.
